options.text: The mass of one mole of a substance
The sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in a formula
The mass of one molecule in grams
The number of atoms in a formula

questions.explanation: Relative formula mass (Mr) is calculated by adding together the relative atomic masses (Ar) of all the atoms shown in the chemical formula.

questions.stem: Calculate the relative formula mass of water (H₂O). [Ar: H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of H₂O = (2 x 1) + 16 = 2 + 16 = 18. There are 2 hydrogen atoms (each Ar = 1) and 1 oxygen atom (Ar = 16).

questions.stem: Calculate the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). [Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
What is the relative formula mass of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂? [Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Mr of Mg(OH)₂ = 24 + 2 x (16 + 1) = 24 + 2 x 17 = 24 + 34 = 58. The brackets mean there are 2 OH groups.

questions.stem: What is relative atomic mass (Ar) measured relative to?

options.text: 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom

questions.explanation: Relative atomic mass is measured relative to 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, which is defined as exactly 12. This provides a standard scale for comparing atomic masses.

questions.stem: Calculate the relative formula mass of sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄). [Ar: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
Why does relative formula mass have no units?

options.text: Because it is a ratio comparing masses to the carbon-12 standard
Because the units have not been decided yet
Because atoms are too small to measure

questions.explanation: Relative formula mass is a ratio - it compares the mass of a formula unit to 1/12 of a carbon-12 atom. Since it is a comparison (a ratio), the units cancel out.
